correctness.rationale: Greedy shortest rich blocks determine the linear index: the sequence of their closing letters followed by a letter absent from the remainder is a missing subsequence, since the earliest possible embeddings of the closing letters are the arch endpoints. Each rich factor supplies an adjacent unlike pair, and k disjoint unlike edges on the odd cycle leave one vertex unmatched; cutting there linearizes all k pairs. Removing the equal edges leaves paths, isolated vertices included. A path with t edges leaves t+1 modulo 2 vertices uncovered by a maximum matching, so maximality means exactly one even t. For counting, distinguish the equal edge after that unique even run. If there are 2h odd runs, the 2h+1 run-plus-terminal-edge lengths have base lengths 2,...,2,1 and even excess; the resulting composition count is binom(k,2h). The sum is 2^(k-1) for k>=1. There are 2k+1 labels for the distinguished edge and two binary lifts of each transition vector. An odd maximizer uses k and k+1 symbols (it must realize both constant targets), so it cannot be a nontrivial power; equivalently, a rotation stabilizing it must fix the distinguished edge. Thus each necklace has 2k+1 distinct origins. The two fixed-origin cases (all arches of length two with one remaining symbol, or one length-three arch) are disjoint by greedy uniqueness and give (k+2)2^k, proving the rescue count by subtraction. The k=1 result and zero-length even runs are included.
